strongest_bounded_proposition: At 1800, metropolitan Britain cannot be summarized as simply slave-society-present or slavery-abolished: metropolitan slavery had largely receded while imperial/Atlantic participation remained extensive.
strongest_unsupported_proposition: Do not infer metropolitan practice from colonial plantation slavery/trade participation or treat Somerset 1772 as simple nationwide abolition.
territorial_practice_summary: Metropolitan slaveholding had become rare/weak by late eighteenth century.
legal_state_summary: Somerset and related cases had narrower effects than a simple abolition label.
external_network_summary: British imperial/Atlantic slavery participation remained major.
terminology_category_qualification: Sample label risks conflating metropole and empire.
temporal_scope_precision: Bounded to cited evidence; sample interval is not itself slavery evidence.
inference_extent: Separate metropolitan practice from colonial/external participation.
language_access_limitations: English-accessible packet only; non-English/non-digitized scholarship not exhaustively searched.
